sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 who is served in the matter, has remained un-represented before this Court.

3. FIR in Crime No.130/2024 was registered by Sindhanoor Town Police Station, Raichur district,
against the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 26.08.2024, received from the respondent No.2 herein, who is the mother of the victim-girl aged 17 years.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation of the case, the petitioner herein was arrested on 05.09.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
The investigation of the case is completed and the charge-sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
His bail application filed before the trial Court in Crl.
Misc. No.5480/2024 was rejected on 08.01.2025.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the victim-girl has not made any allegation against the NC: 2025:KHC-K:823 petitioner in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, which would attract the alleged offences.
He submits that, though the victim-girl was found missing from her house from the month of June, 2023 itself, the first informant had not approached the police till 26.08.2024.
The petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.

6. The first informant who is the mother of the victim-girl aged about 17 years has submitted typed first information on 26.08.2024, based on which an FIR in Crime No.130/2024 came to be registered against the petitioner.
In the said first information, it is stated that, her minor daughter aged 17 years was found missing from their house in the month of June, 2023.
Efforts made to trace her had failed.
Since her elder daughter had eloped with somebody earlier, she did not make any further attempts to search her missing daughter.

On the NC: 2025:KHC-K:823 intervening night of 16.08.2024 and 17.08.2024, at about 1.00 a.m., she received a phone call from the mother of the petitioner herein, stating that, her daughter who is the victim in the present case, was pregnant by nine months and she is being taken to hospital for delivery.
Thereafter, the first informant went to the Hospital and found that, her missing daughter was pregnant and admitted in the hospital.
It is in this background, she has approached the police on 26.08.2024, after her daughter gave birth to the child, alleging that, the petitioner was the cause for the pregnancy of her daughter.
7. Statement of the victim-girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., has been recorded in the present case by the jurisdictional Magistrate.
The victim-girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner in the said statement, which would attract the charge-sheeted offence against him.
Undisputedly, the petitioner has no other criminal antecedents.
The investigation of the case is completed and the charge-sheet has been filed.
Therefore, I am of NC: 2025:KHC-K:823 the opinion that, his prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
